newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analysts comments on Credit Lyonnais.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Credit Lyonnais.

text.p: The following are analysts' comments on state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais, for which the French government is due shortly to announce terms of a new rescue package.

The comments were made in interviews with Reuters Financial Television before an announcement by the European Commission that it did not expect to receive the rescue plan on Friday. French government sources had said earlier the European Commission would get the plan this week.
SAMI GOTRANE, ANALYST AT FRENCH BROKERS EIFB
-- What do you think the government is likely to suggest as a rescue plan to the European Commission?
I think the first point will be to sell BfG, the German affiliate of Credit Lyonnais, because it is the only sacrifice that the Credit Lyonnais will be authorised to make.
The second point will be recapitalisation.
I think that some banks or perhaps insurance companies in the world will be interested in the acquisition of Credit Lyonnais.
-- What about the estimate of a 30 billion francs cost to get Credit Lyonnais in shape?
I think it is a very high estimate. My own estimate is more like 20 billion francs, because of the loss on BfG and also the recapitalisation solution, which will be very important.
-- On the opposition to the rescue plan by rival Societe Generale, which has suggested a "controlled liquidation"?

It is perhaps the right way in order to protect the margins for Societe Generale as a competitor of Credit Lyonnais on the French market. But for the national community, for the French state for example, the social cost of such a measure will be so high that it would lead to political problems.
-- Do you think the privatisation could come up soon ?

I think if the Brussels Commission agrees to the latest rescue plan, things will happen very fast. It will be difficult with the euro and all the coming changes to maintain a public bank like Credit Lyonnais.
JEAN-BAPTISTE BELLON, ANALYST, DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL

-- The French banking system is a non-profit making system, with hugely excessive capital in mutual banks and a very old culture of doing banking like an administration, something you can use as a taxpayer. It is not really a corporate thing. That explains a lot of the weakness of the banking sector.
-- What reform is needed?

The first point is a more open playing field between commercial banks and mutual banks, the second is to liberalise tight social regulations, the third is to allow French banks to have a normal way of making money, with payment of services. The use of cheque payment is free for customers, and costly for banks.
-- Would a privatised Credit Lyonnais have a viable future?
If reshaped as a French domestic bank on the French retail market, really it would be ok, but it would pay for the cost of selling European businesses.
Reshaped, it can be a viable, small original French bank, but for the long run it should be backed by another regional European bank.
Credit Lyonnais could maintain market share if it cuts costs, they have a good quality of assets now, I think they can compete in this way.
The first thing would be to create a new, good player on the regional scene rather than breaking up Credit Lyonnais.
-- Laura Geoffroy Paris Newsroom +33 1 42 21 53 81
